Subject: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler — post-demo recap + next steps

Hi Jessica (and Carlos),

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: validate performance, cost, and reliability tradeoffs for your retrieval-gen pipeline at 1M monthly requests, with 99th percentile latency target <300ms for single-turn generation.
- What we showed: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + autoscaling + prefix caching) vs a hyperscaler-managed GPU endpoint (burst/spot-backed). Key differentiators we called out: predictable throughput and capacity guarantees on Dedicated; built-in KV/prefix caching and batching optimizations that reduce token cost; and our rollout/fallback policies for regional failover.

Attachments: we included a one-pager and a suggested POC test plan (attached). Rafael — I included a rough cost-model estimate as well.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) ACME to run two short tests in our POC -- a) stability/stress test (24-hour sustained 100 TPS for cold-start heavy workloads) and b) latency distribution test (2000 randomized requests to measure p50/p95/p99).
2) Redwood to provision a Dedicated demo pool sized for the tests (reserved nodes) and provide an equivalent hyperscaler test config (we'll help you template infra on Azure/GCP for parity).
3) Share contract/pricing guidance so procurement can evaluate reserved commitment vs pay-as-you-go hyperscaler spend.
4) Quick sync next week to finalize test windows.

Ask: Jessica — can you confirm the POC owner on your side and preferred test dates (we suggested 7/21–7/23 for the stress window)?

Best,
Markus

Hi Jessica — quick follow-up with the requested items. Attached is an initial apples-to-apples cost model (cost-model-estimates.xlsx) and the POC test plan doc with exact API endpoints we'll use. High level:

- Dedicated (reserved 12-mo commitment for demo-sized pool): predictable monthly charge with guaranteed baseline capacity. For the POC we commit to the provisioned pool being available and able to sustain the reserved throughput; we will also provide a documented fallback policy (automatic regional fallback to a compatible model variant) in the unlikely event of local capacity issues.
- Hyperscaler PAYG: variable spend that can be lower if workload variability is high, but no capacity reservation — during spikes you can hit quota limits or need to coordinate larger reserved VM buys with the hyperscaler which adds procurement friction.

SLA/Capacity specifics for the POC:
- Baseline availability for the reserved nodes: 99.5% for POC window (we can discuss enterprise SLA for production separately).
- We will guarantee baseline throughput equal to the provisioned pool capacity for the POC timeframe. If we observe sustained saturation during the test we will: a) provide temporary burst capacity where feasible, or b) pause the test and conduct joint root-cause analysis.

I'll be on the 7/21 kickoff and will coordinate provisioning; Lauren, can you confirm internal onboarding steps (access, keys, Runbook link)?

Rafael
